source.description: An information exchange package (IEP) description is a collection of artefacts that define and describe the structure and content of an IEP. An Information Exchange Package Documentation has a specific information exchange context and may refer to other semantic assets.
A mapping is a relationship between a concept in one vocabulary and one or more concepts in another.
A name authority list is a controlled vocabulary for use in naming particular entities consistently.
An ontology is a formal, explicit specification of a shared conceptualisation.
A schema is a concrete view on a system or information exchange, describing the structure, content and semantics of data.
A service description is a set of documents that describe the interface to and semantics of a service.
source.provenance: Web Services Glossary – W3C Working Group Note – 11 February 2004

source.description: Statistical data is data which holds information that is of a statistical nature.

source.description: Syntax Encoding Schemes indicate that the value is a string formatted in accordance with a formal notation, such as "2000-01-01" as the standard expression of a date.
A taxonomy is a scheme of categories and subcategories that can be used to sort and otherwise organise items of knowledge or information.

A thesaurus is a controlled and structured vocabulary in which concepts are represented by terms, organised so that relationships between concepts are made explicit, and preferred terms are accompanied by lead-in entries for synonyms or quasi-synonyms.
An application profile is a profile which specifies and describes the metadata used in a particular application.
Style sheets are a set of rules which describes the presentation of a document written in a markup language.

Geospatial data is data that has explicit geographic positioning information included within it in either vector or raster format.

Test data is data which is created for use in tests, which should be syntactically correct but which may not necessarily represent any real-world phenomena, e.g. datasets with ‘dummy data’, typically used in system integration.

Synthetic data is data which is (artificially) created entirely or partially for use in tests, and to meet specific needs or conditions in the real-world that (existing) real-world data may not represent, e.g. anonymised datasets, typically used for proof of concept or simulation.
A glossary is a simple list of terms and their definitions. A glossary focuses on creating a complete list of the terminology of domain-specific terms and acronyms.

A directory contains information about individual entities (e.g. persons) and their (probably) hierarchical organisation and related entities. It is used to browse individuals in their organisational context.
